findings.reason: a node will find its negative control ("the first fixture at the base revision gives review-missing") does not reproduce, so the plan must name the condition that actually failed (record-path resolution or the head-suffixed durable fallback) or the node either duplicates an existing recognition or lands with no reproducible defect.
findings.text: §16 says the pointer's null `reviewed_run_id`/`review_subject` meant "the in-flight reading could not tie it to the run it reviews", and prescribes recognition "through `recovery_review_delivery._resolved_reviewed_run_id`", but that resolver is already the in-flight reader's own fallback: `recovery_review_dispatch._review_subject` (:331-358) returns it when no granted record path names a run, and `_review_in_flight` (:491-560, reached from `obligations._in_flight_review`:411) already sweeps every live review pointer through `_review_subject`; neither field the section blames is read on that path, so the mechanism it prescribes is present at HEAD

findings.reason: without naming the pane word or carried kind, a node satisfies only half its own done-when and the pane the section exists for still prints nothing.
findings.text: §17 says the release "writes one row to the project's watch stream, naming both hosts, and the pane carries it once", but the pane prints only rows `ticker.stream_carries` passes (ticker.py:1391-1419): a pane word in `CARRIED_PANE_WORDS` (:488), a launch or landing mark, or a `ROW_COORDINATOR` class; a seat-release row has no `PANE_STATES` word at all (`PANE_STATES`, :383-437), so `_pane_word` returns "" and the row is withheld, and the section names no word, carried-kind membership or coordinator class to add although it grants `ticker.py`

findings.reason: the rule as scoped trades one wrong row for a missing real one on the resume path §3 and §14 both produce, so the plan needs the per-attempt key and an arm that proves the resumed attempt's delivery still prints.
findings.text: §15's rule suppresses "a delivery the pane already showed … once that run's `in review` row has been drawn", keyed to the row policy's per-run memory with no attempt boundary, while its only guard is "a new attempt's launch after it still prints"; after a resume the new attempt launches (printing), then delivers again with the same word, so a literal implementation drops that attempt's genuine delivery, and no arm in the done-when feeds launch-after-review followed by that attempt's own delivery

findings.reason: the next build beat would read an open followup directing it at three completed sections and would not learn that §15–§17 are the remaining work.
findings.text: the open followup `f-alwh-004` still recommends `/reckon-build a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted §14` and orders "§14 comes first, then §5 and then §7 … then §13 … §11 last", but §14 closed at 2026-10-24T22:10Z (`c-close-s14`), §5 at 23:20Z and §7 at 2026-10-25T01:05Z, all three declared `done` in `plan-section-declarations`, and the followup neither drops them nor names §15–§17

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §15's suppression rule has no attempt boundary and its done-when has no arm for the resumed attempt's own delivery.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each new section records its gate and its negative control in the node's gate log, and §11's report path is the durable evidence fragment directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new sections introduce no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers; `in review` and `seat release` are data words, not section IDs.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §16's stated cause is not what the cited reading does (the node-id resolver is already its fallback), and §17's mechanism names no way for the pane to carry the row it writes.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15, §16 and §17 each name one deliverable (a row-policy suppression, an in-flight review recognition plus its pointer field, a seat-release row).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the open followup f-alwh-004 still recommends `/reckon-build … §14` and an order whose first three sections are `done`.
